newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-EBRD profits as east Europe matures.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-EBRD profits as east Europe matures.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), which was set up in 1991 to aid the transition of central and eastern Europe to the market economy, is seeing higher levels of income from its investments as markets in the region mature.

The EBRD said on Wednesday that profit from the sale of equity investments was 4.33 million Ecu ($5.54 million) in the nine months to end-September, up from just 112,000 Ecu a year ago. Dividend income was 7.7 million Ecu, up from 5.7 million.

"Dividend income from our equity portfolio is now becoming a regular phenomenon for the bank and exit gains are now a structural part of our accounts," Bart le Blanc, vice president of the EBRD said in an interview.
Equity investments now account for a quarter of the development bank's portfolio.

Interest from the bank's loan and debt portfolio was 141 million Ecu against 128.3 million a year earlier. The bank made a net profit of 2.2 million Ecu after stiff provisions of 67.5 million Ecus, compared with a net loss of 1.8 million a year ago.
Operating profit before provisions surged 63 percent to 69.7 million Ecu.
The bank tends to take provisions at the start of projects, a policy which was necessitated by its expansion into the less developed markets of Russia and the former Soviet Union.
"There is a shift towards the eastern part of our region and Russia in particular saw a larger increase in activity than elsewhere," le Blanc said.
EBRD's commitments rose to 1.1 billion Ecu in the first nine months of this year, compared with 918 million in the year ago period. Disbursements of money rose to 898 million from 750 million.
For the full year, the bank expects to report a small profit after provisions and noted that its costs, which have been a bugbear in the past, have stabilised.
In April this year, the nations which contribute to the bank agreed to double its capital to 20 billion Ecu so it could expand its operations in the eastern part of the region.
The key to obtaining that concession was an agreement to keep costs steady while expanding operations.

"It is clear that our portfolio will keep on growing. The capital increase commits us to investments of 2.0-2.5 billion Ecu a year," le Blanc said. -- David Chance London newsroom 44 171 542 5887 ($1=.7810 Ecu)
